summary: All three occurrences are already quoted in the entry. No new example, sense or box is needed; the revised entry preserves the existing numbered senses and Detransitive distinction.

63/144 has God as the overt permitting agent, the couple as a suffix-coded patient and ʕal ḥḏoḏe as the reciprocal relation. It remains active II Infectum, not Detransitive merely because the German uses an allowed-state expression.

107/151 and 113/219 have the couple or spouse as the state/change bearer, without an overt permitting agent. The former is Detransitive Preterit with aʕle; the latter is Detransitive Infectum under ḥatta d- with ʕal ḥḏoḏe.
Marital licitness is already represented by the existing legal-permission sense; do not split off a separate 'marry' sense or add an idiom solely from the surrounding wedding narrative.
The source identification ḥly 2 is preserved; none of these occurrences supports conflation with another homonymous root.

Does 107/151 specifically restore an earlier lawful marriage, or simply establish the other woman as a lawful spouse? The supplied verse establishes licitness but does not by itself settle the prior legal history.
